**Observations from the image:**

- **Affected part:** Banana leaf
- **Lesion characteristics:**
  - A single, well-defined oval/elliptical lesion centrally positioned on the leaf
  - Dark brown to black center (necrotic core)
  - Surrounded by a distinct orange-yellow halo ring
  - The surrounding leaf tissue remains green and healthy
  - The lesion has clear, defined margins

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Cordana Leaf Spot:** Caused by *Cordana musae*, produces oval/elliptical lesions with a dark brown center surrounded by a yellow-orange halo on banana leaves — this matches very well.
- **Yellow and Black Sigatoka:** Typically produces streaks that evolve into elongated lesions with yellow halos, often with gray-white centers and dark margins — possible but the shape here is more rounded/oval than streaky.
- **Anthracnose:** Usually affects fruits (post-harvest) with sunken dark lesions, less typical on leaves with this pattern.
- **Panama Disease, Banana Bunchy Top Virus, Bunchy Top, Cigar End Rot:** These affect different plant parts or show very different symptoms (wilting, streaking on leaves/pseudostems, tip rot of fruit).

The single, oval lesion with a jet-black necrotic center and prominent yellow-orange halo on a leaf is a hallmark of **Cordana Leaf Spot**.
